findings: UserData defaults SameContents and SameSize to true, across-directories true, hidden/system exclusion true. Thus JPEG transformation is paired by default with original encoded-size equality, narrowing which differing metadata files can match; equal-length differing leading APP payloads still satisfy this size gate. UI mapping remains unread.

Serialized duplicate-file records contain path, group, marks, locks and metadata but no content digest, physical identity, recipe version or observation stamp. Actual save/load mapping and validation remain unread.

IFileService.MoveToRecycleBin returns bool, but reviewed FinderService.DeleteFilesAsync ignores it. Both platform implementations here return true after a nonthrowing call; Windows requests UICancelOption.DoNothing, so cancellation outcome needs runtime verification.

Linux trash uses hardcoded ~/.local/share/Trash, ignoring XDG_DATA_HOME and external-volume trash selection. Collision checks examine only files, not existing .trashinfo; WriteAllText can overwrite orphan metadata. Metadata is written before File.Move, with no cleanup if the move fails. No trash operation executed.

Windows icon cache keys executable files by basename rather than full path, so two different executables with the same name can reuse an icon. Folder/extension caches have no bound or explicit invalidation/disposal in this class.
Linux previews decode a bitmap directly from file, without a size limit visible here. Windows previews use a fixed 256-pixel request but underlying extraction and image disposal remain to inspect.
limitations: Source review only for platform operations; no launch, trash, desktop integration or preview executed
